\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ورزشگاه} (varzeshgâh)}{ورزشگاه (varzeshgâh)}]{\fa{ورزشگاه} (varzeshgâh) — a stadium}

\label{lesson:FA-C267-varzeshgah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an entrance, then the Persian for an exit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ورزشگاه}}
\textbf{\fa{ورزشگاه}} — \emph{varzeshgâh} — \textquotedblleft{}a stadium\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{varzeshgâh} is built from \emph{varzesh}, \textquotedblleft{}sport, exercise\textquotedblright{} (from \emph{varzidan}, \textquotedblleft{}to practise\textquotedblright{}), and \emph{gâh}, \textquotedblleft{}place\textquotedblright{}: the place of sport. \emph{varzidan} is inherited, usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{warzīdan}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{varzeshgâh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{varzeshgâh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{varzeshgâh}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an entrance, then the Persian for an exit, then say \emph{varzeshgâh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{ورزشگاه} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A stadium\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پایتخت} (pâytakht)}{پایتخت (pâytakht)}]{\fa{پایتخت} (pâytakht) — a capital city}

\label{lesson:FA-C267-paytakht}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an exit, then the Persian for a stadium.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پایتخت}}
\textbf{\fa{پایتخت}} — \emph{pâytakht} — \textquotedblleft{}a capital city\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pâytakht} is \emph{pâ}, \textquotedblleft{}foot\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{takht}, \textquotedblleft{}throne\textquotedblright{}: the foot of the throne, the seat of the ruler. Both are inherited; \emph{takht} continues Middle Persian \emph{taxt} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مرز} (marz)}{مرز (marz)}]{\fa{مرز} (marz) — a border}

\label{lesson:FA-C267-marz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a stadium, then the Persian for a capital city.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مرز}}
\textbf{\fa{مرز}} — \emph{marz} — \textquotedblleft{}a border\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{marz} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{marz}, \textquotedblleft{}border\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB takes it back to the Indo-European root \emph{*mereǵ-}, \textquotedblleft{}edge, boundary\textquotedblright{}, the root usually also given for English \emph{mark}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{صخره} (sakhre)}{صخره (sakhre)}]{\fa{صخره} (sakhre) — a rock, a cliff}

\label{lesson:FA-C267-sakhre}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a capital city, then the Persian for a border.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{صخره}}
\textbf{\fa{صخره}} — \emph{sakhre} — \textquotedblleft{}a rock, a cliff\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sakhre} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṣaḫra}, \textquotedblleft{}rock, great stone\textquotedblright{}. Its Arabic root is \emph{ṣ-ḫ-r} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اقیانوس} (oqyânus)}{اقیانوس (oqyânus)}]{\fa{اقیانوس} (oqyânus) — an ocean}

\label{lesson:FA-C267-oqyanus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a border, then the Persian for a rock.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اقیانوس}}
\textbf{\fa{اقیانوس}} — \emph{oqyânus} — \textquotedblleft{}an ocean\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{oqyânus} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ūqiyānūs}, which goes back to Greek \emph{ōkeanos}, the great outer sea (EtymDB). English \emph{ocean} is the same Greek word.
\end{cousinweb}
